sections.content:
The course is talking about wireless communication technology. I think it teach deeper and further about the context of Elec 3100, It was mainly talking about different application of communication, through Gaussian distribution and Q function, like 16QAM as an example.
Still, the context of the technology is very hard to understand and need extra time to learn. For me as example, it take me many hours to revision and understand the enode for transimission for communiaction
sections.teaching:
Professor Lau teach us very well about the course materials. He can  explain complicated concept clearly and easier to understand than on note. With the more difficult concept he will explain on white board. He also weclomed to be asked and answer a lot of question for me.
The two PG TAs, their teaching style is not that good. They mainly just talk directly from the PPT in the tutorial, making their tutorial is hard to remember. Still, they will like to answer my qurstion about the PPT after the tutorial. Still, there wdoes not have new things can learn in tutorial besides the tutorial notes, so just look at it is ok.
sections.grading:
the grading is a little harsh. I remember the final exam mean is lower than 50, and the final exam is kind of hard for me.
One thing that is worth to mention is that the deadline of their final project have been push early for around 12 hours. And they mention  the change of deadline for like 1 day before.Therefore I was unprepared about the deadline and cannot submit my project on time, thus my work on project was been wasted.
sections.workload:
several homework,one project and 2 exams.
Actually not very much work needed to do.
project is not that hard to do, homework need to use the techiques in tutorial notes.
Just may need to study a lot for the exam as the question is quite hard.

sections.content: Mainly about wireless communication technology. Can be regarded as an upgraded version of elec 3100, with high emphasis on the application of Gaussian distribution and Q function.
sections.teaching:
Professor Lau gave a clear and thorough explanation on white board. His demonstration helped us to understand the concepts well with confidence and interest in digging deeper into communication technology.

But the PG TAs, especially Zhuang Jialin and Zhai Tianyi indeed had shitwood teaching needs.

Zhai Tianyi refused to grade the homework until the very last week of the semester. He even advanced the deadline for a group project right in one day before the new deadline, making us very rushed to finish it.  His tutorials applied a very low volume of sound that even the first row students complained that no one can hear a word. He even refused to answer email unless the sender emailed Prof. Lau for it. He went to the wrong exam venue, leaving the SEN students no monitor so they had to delay their exam to another schedule.

Zhuang Jialin knew very little about wireless communication and in tutorials, she had to ask AI before answer some very basic questions. She designed the midterm exam paper but she herself didn’t know how to answer it. She just paraphrased some past paper and homework questions and asked AI to generate the answer for it. In one question, to calculate the Fourier Transform of a sin function, when it added 2 pi, Zhuang Jialin didn’t know it was actually the same answer as no 2 i added, and then she thought the question was wrongly designed, and thus, she gave everyone full mark. We had to appeal very hard to get the question well graded. If we students need to fight for this small issues, why do we need PG TAs?

The most awful stuff is when Zhuang Jialin designed the midterm paper, she chose not to lay emphasis on elec 4110 content at all. This is indeed typical behavior of shitwood teaching needs. She put 75% of the contents in the domain of elec 2100, say for example, 10 marks for one convolution, and another 10 marks, just to flip the input signal and redo the convolution. What kind of <kaml> can design this shit to humiliate us students? In the end, the midterm mean was very low, around 38/100. Thanks to her good job!

Zhuang Jialin and Zhai Tianyi could not finish the final paper grading within one week. In comparison, elec 3100 can finish grading right in the same day of final exam before 11:59 pm! This can prove that it is not the workload is too much, it is simply Zhuang and Zhai were too lazy or had skill issue to do their jobs well. This led to the result that, we had no paper checking session at all. Shame on them!

By name spelling, you can easily identify that Zhuang and Zhai are Gaokao students from mainland. Gaokao students, I won't say everyone, but many of them have a high exam grade but low skill potential. It is totally fine that these people want to shit their own life, but it is not acceptable to bring their shitwoodness to us students, while getting paid around 20k hkd per month, a large part of which actually might come from the tuition fee of us ugs!

Sometimes Zhuang and Zhai complained that the attendance was too low. Why not go to check the same school, MY's tutorial? How can't you learn from MY and Vivian to know at least how to do your job well? I have to say your shit teaching skills deserve this low attendance rate, coz you never put a shit on your job and have no sense of duty at all!

To keep these PG TAs like Zhuang and Zhai is to put mud on UST's fame. I highly recommend every student who want to take this course, prepare yourself to do self-study instead of going to the shit TA tutorials, which can only waste your time, focus and energy with the only gain in the end is to give you emotional damage.

Rely on yourself, not the TAs! Go get A+ and this will give a load slap on those shit TAs face, which can be proved a victory of UG godwoods fighting against the virus of PG shitwoods. Add oil! You are the best!
sections.grading: It is good. I believe it is 25%, thanks to generosity of Mr. Lau.
sections.workload: Median. With homeworks, midterm, final, and group project. Some of the workload was spent on appealing with professor who sometimes went on vacation, and mostly on the TAs.

sections.content:
Ch 1: Introductions (Brief revisit on ELEC 2100 Signals and Fourier Transform)
Ch 2: Review on Digital Modulation (Heavily involves probability & Q function)
Ch 3: Signal Space (ppl say it's similar to ELEC 3100, which I didn't take. It's quite easy to grasp if you also have foundations on MATH2111)

Ch 4: M General M-ary Mod/Demodulation
Ch 6: MFSK Error Analysis
Ch 7: MQAM Error Analysis (also covers MPSK)
(Midterm covers up to Ch 7)

Ch 9: Small-scale fading
Ch 10:Diversity Techniques
Ch 11: ISI Mitigation
Ch 12: Resource Partitioning
Ch 13: Case study (basically a review on the history of the cellular system, not really relevant in the exam)

At first, it was hard to grasp due to my weakness in mathematics, not to mention how they also cover random variables and random processes from ELEC2600 (which I also did not take). It was quite rough with the amount of equations and computational stuff. And I felt like the content post mid-term is so what better than pre mid-term
sections.teaching: Vincent preferred to focus on understanding the concepts in practice rather than memorising the equations. He does encourage all to attend lectures, and I did. It does take a while to grasp these concepts, and it does help when I actively take notes and organise them into diagrams to visualize them better
sections.grading:
Homework (5% each *3)   15%
Midterm 25%
Project 10%
Finals Exam 50%

I got 75, 70 & 96 out of 100 for the 3 HW. 90/100 for the project.

The midterm was horrible, 27/100 (It was an exam during lecture time, and we had Tue/Thurs 9 am ), with the Fourier transform table given halfway thru the exam + I wasn't prepared. The majority of the class got 20 - late 30/ early 40-ish, and only a few managed to reach 70 or above.

Final scores aren't released yet, so I'll probably update later
sections.workload:
The HWs are manageable; most can be easily dealt with when you have the slides beside you as a reference. They didn't talk much about the project until two-thirds of the semester had passed. They did provide a general framework as a reference, and MATLAB was alright.

For the exams, you can bring one handwritten double-sided A4-size cheat sheet for the Midterm and two for the finals. The lookup table for Q-function, and the Fourier transform table (only some, not all), will be provided.

sections.content:
Representation of signals, optimum detection of signals in noise, matched filtering, error probability calculations for digital modulation. Multilevel modulation schemes, comparison of digital communications systems, mobile and wireless channels, diversity techniques, spread-spectrum communications, Resource Partitioning in Multiuser systems (FDMA, TDMA, CDMA) and their applications in cellular mobile and wireless personal communications.
Definitely take it if you are going for communications.
sections.teaching: Vincent's teaching is super nice and clear.
sections.grading: Would update when the results come out. But I heard that Vincent is super nice in terms of grading so I would not worry that much.
sections.workload:
The assignments are not that hard.
The exam is quite similar to the assignments.

sections.content:
review of Fourier transform, matched filter, signal space from 3100 (but you need to how those works in math forms now. Follow what Vincent taught will be good enough).
Then expand to m-ary, fading channel, diversity, spread spectrum (RAKE) intro to OFDM, and resource partition (FDMA, CDMA, and CDMA)

Case study seems to differ every year, just some hot topics for fun.

The whole course is still basic content of digital communication but really a good introduction. The mathematics for bit error rate is of importance and only simple calculation is needed for fading channel (I spend weeks dealing with the math of fading channels of different distribution but none is tested at the end)
sections.teaching:
Vincent will stress on understanding first and then fill up proofs with math.
You'd better not miss any of the lectures. It takes longer to understand what is going. Vincent could explain everything clearly and efficiently.

The reference book is helpful.
The wireless communication by Vincent is of good quality for understanding. If you want to know more and elaborate with more math, Proakis-digital-CDMA recommended.

sections.workload:
It depends. 85% of exams are similar to homework and may be easier but you need to be careful to obtain all those marks.

Only the last questions of midterm and final is challenging and require you to have a deep understanding but these problems really test if you can handle the practical issue.

Sincerely to take 30-40 minutes to integrate what you learn every week. You can get a solid understanding and life is easy. All content is quite connected.

the project is simple and helpful for understanding the process of communication. Just need few codes

homework will be elaborated in the tutorial and TA(Terry, HE, Tierui is super nice!!!) will help you patiently and help you understand the nature of the question.
